channel.title: LoomSci - Artificial Intelligence
channel.description: Latest Artificial Intelligence articles from LoomSci

item.title: The Safety Constraint Hiding Outside the Data
item.description: In a model's training distribution, the safety boundary is a hole: nothing in the data marks where a sandbox escape begins, so the constraint must be verified from outside.

item.title: Turning AI Inward to Dissect Its Own Beliefs
item.description: An autonomous AI system turns interpretability methods on a language model, mapping its internal beliefs and steering its behavior from within.

item.title: Proving the Unprovable: Certifying AI’s Probabilistic Consistency
item.description: An interactive proof verifier spot-checks an AI's web of probabilistic predictions against a compact proof oracle, ensuring all its answers could come from one coherent worldview.

item.title: Reading a Burnt Chip’s Memory: The Crash Data That Refused to Die
item.description: Floating-gate memory cells retain their charge pattern even after a chip's silicon is melted, allowing forensic recovery of crash data with a scanning electron microscope.

item.title: When 'Stop' Doesn't Mean Stop: The Enforcement Gap in AI Agents
item.description: When an AI agent's approval gate pauses one branch, a concurrent sibling can still leak side effects; an external reference monitor re-establishes true stop.

item.title: The Optical Fibre Learns to Cancel Its Own Echoes
item.description: A new CP-OFDM waveform cancels spatial inter-symbol interference in distributed acoustic sensing, eliminating phantom echoes from Rayleigh backscattered light.

item.title: When Robots Learn to Plan in Chapters
item.description: Hierarchical planning enables a robot to compose long tasks into compressed macro-actions, achieving 70% success where flat planning fails entirely.

item.title: Painting Radio Fields: How Point Clouds Extrapolate the Invisible
item.description: 3D Gaussian scatterers on LiDAR point clouds extrapolate angular power spectra, painting invisible radio fields across entire city grids.

item.title: When the Judge Is on Trial: Second-Order Bias in Language Models
item.description: When a machine is asked to judge bias, its own internal social map may tip the scales—second-order bias hides in the act of judgment itself.

item.title: Escaping the Incentive Collapse: Why AI Must Learn to Stumble
item.description: To prevent humans from passively trusting perfect AI, researchers propose injecting deliberate errors—"sentinels"—that reward vigilance, breaking the incentive collapse.

item.title: Learning to Generate Rare Events from Topological Fingerprints
item.description: A neural network learns to generate realistic rare events by reading the hidden topological fingerprints—like loops and voids—in data's persistent homology.
